newsitem.title: USA: Dow falls, Nasdaq streak ends amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Dow falls, Nasdaq streak ends amid profit-taking.

text.p: Wall Street paused in its record-shattering run on Thursday, pulling blue chips slightly lower and sending Nasdaq to its first loss in two weeks.

The Dow fell 18 points to close unofficially at 8021, a day after its first breach of the 8,000 point barrier. The Nasdaq Composite fell 12 points to 1569, snapping a 10 session winning streak that matched its longest this decade.
"We needed this. We needed room to breathe," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capital markets at Cruttenden Roth.
"Right now, things are in the stratosphere."
The Dow's decline came despite a powerful rally by component Merck & Co Inc, which surged 8-1/4 to 106-3/4 after reporting strong second quarter earnings and sales.
The performance was a mirror image of Wednesday's, when the blue chip average overcame a severe sell-off in component Eastman Kodak Co after disappointing earnings.
"What we're seeing is investors saying they may sell Kodak because they don't like the earnings, or buy Merck because they do," said Richard Cripps chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
"What we're not seeing is evidence that money is leaving the market," Cripps said.

Broad market indicators showed mild weakness, with the S&P 500 and NYSE Composite retreating from record levels. By far the stiffest profit-taking took place in the tech sector, where recent gains have been the most dramatic.

The group may come under new pressure on Friday, following Microsoft Corp's fourth quarter earnings report, released after the close. Microsoft earned $0.80 per share in the quarter, beating Wall Street estimates by a penny.
Analysts said, however, that Microsoft's sprint from a price of 130 to nearly 150 per share in barely a week suggested the market had expected more from the software giant.
"Considering the run we'd seen, coming in at $0.80 when the consensus was $0.79 is not going to do it," said Bill Meehan, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
"This might serve to put some pressure on the market, particularly the large cap tech stocks," he said.
Shares in Microsoft traded lower in after-hours activity, falling to 146 from a closing price of 149-1/2.

Among individual issues, Woolworth Corp jumped 2-1/2 to 27-9/16 after announcing it would close all its general merchandise stores in the U.S., converting some to its more successful specialty athletics format.
The company, named for founder Frank W. Woolworth, also said it plans to change its name later this year.
Raychem Corp leaped 13-3/8 to 90-1/16 after reporting higher fourth quarter earnings late Wednesday. Early today, Merrill Lynch upgraded the stock to outperform.
Louisiana Land and Exploration Co surged 7-3/8 to 65-5/8.

The company agreed to be acquired by Burlington Resources Inc in a stock deal valued at $3 billion under which Burlington will swap 1.525 shares for each Louisiana Land share. Shares in Burlington Resources fell 1-3/4 to 44-3/8.

Octel Communications Corp rose 3-3/8 to 30-1/8 after the voice messaging company agreed to be acquired by Lucent Technologies Inc for $31 per share cash, or $1.8 billion. Lucent, which said it would record an unspecified charge in connection with the deal, fell 2-5/8 to 86-1/16.
The S&P 500 fell 4.98 points to 931.61.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 11.78 points to 1568.85.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
